chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from Muhammad ibn Sinān, from Ya‘qūb Al-Sarrāj, who said:

I entered upon Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام) while he was standing at the head of Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā, and he was in the cradle. He continued speaking privately to him for a long time, so I sat until he had finished. Then I rose toward him, and he said to me, “Come near to your master and greet him.” So I approached and greeted him, and he returned the greeting to me in an eloquent tongue.

Then he said to me, “Go and change the name of your daughter whom you named yesterday, for it is a name that Allah hates.” A daughter had been born to me, and I had named her Al-Humayrā’. So Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام) said, “Comply with his command and you will be rightly guided.” So I changed her name.

key_terms.الْحُمَيْرَاءِ: the specific name given to the daughter, which was ordered to be changed
key_terms.الْمَهْدِ: the cradle in which the infant Imam was lying
key_terms.فَغَيِّرِ: change it, an instruction to alter the child’s name
key_terms.مَوْلَاكَ: your master, referring to the authority and rank of the Imam
key_terms.يُبْغِضُهُ اللَّهُ: Allah dislikes it, indicating the name is detested

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith show about Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) in infancy and changing a disliked child’s name?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter with Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام) and the infant Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā (عليه السلام), in which the child speaks eloquently and gives instruction regarding a disliked name. The report indicates the special status and divinely granted knowledge of the Imam, while also showing obedience to the Imam’s guidance in family matters such as naming a child.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Yaqoub Al Sarraj who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had paused by the head of Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the cradle. So he<sup>asws</sup> went on to talk secretively to him<sup>asws</sup> for a long time. So I sat down until he<sup>asws</sup> was free. Then I stood up to (speak with) him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach your Master<sup>asws</sup>, and greet’. So I approached and greeted upon him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> returned the greeting by an eloquent tongue.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Go, and change the name of your daughter which you named her with yesterday, for it is a name Hated by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. And it was so that a daughter had been born unto me. I had named her as Al-Humeyra. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Finalise this matter, you would be rightly Guided’. So I changed her name’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ya‘qub al-Sarraj who has said the following.

“Once I went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who was standing by the cradle of abu al-Hassan. He began to speak secretly to him for a long time. I sat there until he was free. I then stood for him and he said to me, “Come close to your Mawla (master and Leader with Divine Authority).” I went close and said greetings. He answered my greetings very clearly

and then he said to me, “Go and change the name of your daughter that you named just yesterday. It is a name makes Allah angry.” A girl was born to us and I had named her al-Humayra’.” Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said to me, “Follow his command you will have the right guidance.” I then changed her name.”
